_comment: Status anti-drift mapping: every claim in website/index.html's Status
section maps to a verifiable repo artifact. The page stays hand-authored;
this file polices it (scripts/check-status-claims.mjs, run in CI).
Semantics: shipped: every listed path must exist / the command must exit
zero. in-progress: verified as NOT shipped: every listed path must be
absent / the command must exit non-zero. Claim text must match the page's
Status list one-to-one per column. A claim on the page with no mapping
entry, or vice versa, is drift.
Every entry names the repository its evidence lives in: repo is spec (this
repository) or platform (the platform's codebase). Evidence paths and
commands are relative to that repository's root.

claims.why: The provider selection point (cloud chosen by config), the zero-cloud 'none' provider, and the local boot the claim cites.
One platform source module per capability named on the page (data-access lives in src/data).
The staged pipeline, its CLI entry, and authoring-time context assembly against the live schema.
The capture contract sources plus at least one committed captured prompt artifact from a real run.
The translation stage, its pinned proposal contract, and the canonical rules the stage prompt consumes.
CERT's charter carries a stamped birth certificate and the Platform Panel web app exists.

The stamped birth certificate, generation 1's exact run report, and the phase-2 evidence: the merged record. Split 2026-09-13 into one entry per part of the former five-part claim so that each part is verified at its own grade; the pending part moved to In progress (a stale 'regeneration pending' line passed green on 2026-09-12 because prose is not verified: only artifacts are).

verify.command: grep -q '^    generation: 2$' packages/trade-mirror/charter.yaml && grep -q 'runReport: ai-generation/runs/trade-mirror-2026-09-12T11-18-39-396Z.json' packages/trade-mirror/charter.yaml && test -f ai-generation/runs/trade-mirror-2026-09-12T11-18-39-396Z.json && test -f docs/pilots/trade-mirror/regeneration-2026-09-12.md

claims.why: Demonstrated on trade-mirror at generation 2: the charter's lineage block says generation 2 and points at the 2026-09-12T11-18-39-396Z run report, that report exists, and the regeneration record with the verification table and claim-strength grades exists. charter check verifies the chain itself; the anti-drift job stays seconds-fast by checking the stamped artifacts.

Recorded at its grade, not higher: A national open data portal live-verified at adapter level on 2026-07-08 (SA-7, on the generation-1 adapter built outside the harness, V-7); an international trade statistics database probed to authentication refusal (SA-7); the fixture-fed demo and failed scheduled runs recovered (V-8). Generation 2 (2026-09-12) regenerated the adapters; that verification was not repeated on them: they are fixture-tested only: which is why the live part sits under In progress.

Two things not yet demonstrated: adapter-level live verification on the generation-2 code, and end-to-end scheduled operation (the only scheduled runs on record, 2026-07-08, all failed; the rendered demo was fixture-fed: V-8). Shipping either means a live-operation record lands under docs/pilots/trade-mirror/live-operation/ (convention declared here); until then that directory must be absent, and its appearance turns this claim red until the page moves it to Shipped.
claims.note: CONVENTION CLAIM (accepted as weak, 2026-09-13, same pattern as the external-pilot proxy): a directory's absence stands in for 'not demonstrated'. When live operation ships, replace this proxy with its actual artifact (the run-history record and the live-verification record) in the same change that moves the claim.

claims.why: The capability-to-schema registry and the three pinned config schemas the gates and charter check enforce. Evidence is in the spec: these four files are the contract the platform consumes.

Spec evidence only: the accountability block exists in the pinned schema and is required on every charter. Shipped July 2026. Narrowed 2026-09-19 when the contract moved to its own repository: a spec entry can see only spec files, so the platform half of the page's sentence (the owner registry the unit resolves against, and the named failures OWNER_UNREGISTERED and OWNER_PLACEHOLDER) is no longer verified by this entry.
claims.note: GRADE NOTE (2026-09-19): before the split this entry also checked governance/org-units.yaml and the two named failure codes in the platform's owner-registry resolver. Those artifacts are in the platform repository. Restoring that evidence means a platform entry for it, which needs its own claim on the page because page and map are one-to-one.

claims.why: Spec evidence only: the schema's routing rule (heightened classifications derive the tier alongside ownership, and only ever raise it). Shipped July 2026. Narrowed 2026-09-19 when the contract moved to its own repository: the authoring rule that classification is always asked of a person lives in the platform (ai-generation/rules/tier-routing.md) and is no longer verified by this entry.
claims.note: GRADE NOTE (2026-09-19): before the split this entry also checked the '## Classification routing' section of the platform's tier-routing rule. Restoring that evidence means a platform entry for it, which needs its own claim on the page because page and map are one-to-one.

claims.why: The named failure code in charter check's review-currency gate. Shipped July 2026.

verify.command: test -f packages/platform/src/cli/integration-conformance.ts && grep -q 'INTEGRATION_UNDECLARED_HOST' packages/platform/src/cli/integration-conformance.ts && grep -q 'INTEGRATION_DECLARED_UNWIRED' packages/platform/src/cli/integration-conformance.ts && grep -q 'runtime truth is phase 2' packages/platform/src/cli/integration-conformance.ts packages/platform/src/cli/check.ts

claims.why: The static outbound-surface gate: an undeclared outbound host is a named failure (INTEGRATION_UNDECLARED_HOST); declared-but-unwired (INTEGRATION_DECLARED_UNWIRED) and statically unresolvable targets (INTEGRATION_DYNAMIC_TARGET) are named warnings, never failures: matching the brief's 'what shipped' text and the gate's code. The gate's own line states the limit ('static detection only; runtime truth is phase 2'); the page says runtime egress verification is not built. Shipped July 2026 (phase 1).

The gate with both named directions (CAPABILITY_DECLARED_UNWIRED, CAPABILITY_UNDECLARED_WIRED) and the test named for the pilot-two identity finding (V-2: identity declared, nothing wired on a worker). Shipped 2026-07-15 (backlog 4). Runtime truth is phase 2, per the gate's own line.
The shared stack module, the alert rules, the deploy/rollback doc, the smoke test, and the workflow that exercised rollback on a local (kind) cluster.
Shipping it means an external pilot record lands under docs/pilots/external/ (convention declared here); until then that directory must be absent.
claims.note: CONVENTION CLAIM (accepted as weak, 2026-07-04; proxy narrowed 2026-07-12): the original proxy was docs/pilots/ absence, which broke exactly as predicted when the INTERNAL pilot-two record landed there (PR #17): the check was red on main from 2026-07-08. Narrowed to docs/pilots/external/, same claim semantics. Still a thin proxy; when the external pilot ships, replace this with its actual artifact.
